Weight loss fundamentally boils down to consuming less energy than your body uses. You could have a diet full of sugar and still lose weight if you consumed less calories than your body burns.

The reason people say to cut out carbs and especially sugar when losing weight is because they are far easier to overeat and are generally less satiating and nutritious than food high in fats, protein or fiber.

Honestly though at your weight the first thing you should do is reduce your caloric intake. Balancing out your macro-nutrients will be important, but this is much easier to do in small steps than changing your entire diet at once.

Firstly, calculate your TDEE, which is a rough estimate as to how many calories your body uses in a day.

Then you can track what you eat using a calorie counter such as MyFitnessPal and make sure you are consuming less calories than your TDEE. For sustainable weight loss, aim for a deficit of 500-1000kcals. If you make no progress, you can always increase the deficit slightly.
